keyboards.summary: 75% wired TMR analog keyboard with true 8 kHz reporting and 39 dual-swap switch beds that can mix analog TMR switches with standard 3/5-pin mechanical switches.

sources.label: Logitech G G512 X 75 product page
Logitech G G512 X versus PRO X TKL RAPID comparison

specs.stockSwitch: TMR analog, linear or tactile; 39 dual-swap beds support standard 3/5-pin mechanical switches
specs.caseMaterial: manufacturer does not publish chassis material on the current product page

platform.note: Logitech documents a 75% wired layout, TMR analog sensing, true 8 kHz report rate, 0.1–4.0 mm analog actuation and 39 Dual Swap switch beds. Hot-swap support is specifically scoped to those 39 beds rather than assumed for every position.

inputFeatures.note: Logitech's comparison material explicitly lists Rapid Trigger and Multi-Point Actuation among G512 X features. Atlas preserves the 8 kHz figure as a report-rate specification, not an independent end-to-end latency measurement.

keyboards.summary: 75% Hall-effect keyboard with hot-swappable HFX V2/V2X magnetic switches, 8 kHz polling, Rapid Trigger, Speed Tap and 0.01 mm actuation adjustment steps.

sources.label: ROG Falchion Ace 75 HE product page
ROG Falchion Ace 75 HE technical specifications

specs.stockSwitch: ROG HFX V2 or HFX V2X Magnetic
specs.caseMaterial: manufacturer does not publish chassis material in the current specification

platform.note: ASUS documents the 75% layout, dimensions, HFX V2/V2X options, hot-swappable ROG HE socket platform and double-shot PBT keycaps.

inputFeatures.note: ASUS publishes 8 kHz polling, Rapid Trigger, 0.1–3.5 mm adjustable actuation, 0.01 mm fine-tuning and Speed Tap. Atlas maps Speed Tap into the SOCD-capable field without treating ASUS's response-time marketing as an independent latency result.

switches.summary: Clicky two-pin Hall-effect switch designed around GEONWORKS' VENOM HE platform, with 35 gf operating force, 55 gf bottom-out and 3.5 mm full travel.

sources.label: GEONWORKS Strike HE switch product page

compatibility: Fully compatible with GEONWORKS VENOM HE PCB; other Hall-effect keyboards may require recalibration and compatibility verification.

specification.note: GEONWORKS publishes clicky Hall-effect operation, 35±5 gf operating force, 55±5 gf bottom-out, 3.5 mm travel, two-pin mounting and factory lubrication.

switches.summary: Closed-bottom Hall-effect linear with a 22 mm spring, 42 gf start force, 54 gf end force and full 4 mm travel, tuned for less wobble and a deeper muted sound.

sources.label: Wooting Lekker Tikken Medium product page

compatibility: Requires a keyboard with Hall sensors; verify magnet orientation and board support before use outside Wooting platforms.

specification.note: Wooting publishes a 42 gf start force, 54 gf end force, 4 mm travel, 22 mm spring and medium factory lubrication.

switches.summary: Damped linear Hall-effect switch with a 33 gf initial force, 45 gf bottom-out, 3.2 mm total travel and factory lubrication for a quieter magnetic-switch build.

sources.label: Gateron Magnetic Jade Silent product page

compatibility: Hall-effect compatibility is board-specific; verify polarity, sensing range and firmware support.

specification.note: Gateron publishes 33±5 gf initial, 45±10 gf bottom-out, 3.2±0.2 mm travel, 125/700 Gs flux at 1.2 mm PCB thickness, factory lubrication and at least 60M keystrokes.

switches.summary: Flat-force Hall-effect linear designed around a published 30 gf initial and 30 gf bottom-out force, with 3.2 mm travel and a lower 570 Gs bottom-out flux target.

sources.label: Gateron Magnetic Jade Attraction product page
Gateron Magnetic Jade Attraction force-profile explainer

compatibility: Hall-effect compatibility is board-specific; the 150–570 Gs flux range differs from many Jade-family switches and should be checked against the target keyboard.

specification.note: Gateron specifies 30±3 gf at both initial and bottom-out positions, 3.2±0.2 mm travel, 150/570 Gs flux at 1.2 mm PCB thickness and factory lubrication.

forceProfile.note: The equal start/end force is a physical force-profile characteristic, not an Atlas ranking or claim that the switch is universally better for gaming.
